source_context.title: OpenAI Software Engineer, Privacy Engineering
source_context.summary: Privacy Engineering scope: user data understood, retained, accessed, and used; inventory, mapping, classification, lineage, retention, deletion, access governance, purpose controls, auditability, lifecycle automation, exceptions, incident response, and production observability.

source_context.title: OpenAI Software Engineer, Privacy & Compliance
source_context.summary: Privacy & Compliance emphasis: backend services enforcing policy-driven access and lifecycle controls, distributed authorization, identity-aware enforcement, policy hooks, schema-level constraints, and continuously verifiable compliance.

source_context.title: OpenAI Software Engineer, Privacy Engineering (Lawful Access)
source_context.summary: Lawful Access emphasis: intake, scoping, authorized retrieval, review, preparation, provenance, least privilege, approval gates, data minimization, human oversight, safe failure, and operator experience.

source_context.title: OpenAI Research Engineer, Privacy
source_context.summary: Privacy research track: differential privacy, federated learning, data memorization, membership inference, model inversion, anonymization, and privacy evaluation.

source_context.title: OpenAI Zero Data Retention and Private Safety Processing
source_context.summary: ZDR/private safety framing: severe-risk pattern detection and safety signals under customer-content minimization; trust boundaries must distinguish readable content from narrow derived safety signals.

source_context.title: OpenAI API data controls
source_context.summary: OpenAI API data controls: API inputs and outputs are not used to train models by default; retention and application-state behavior vary by endpoint and setting; ZDR-eligible use requires avoiding persisted application state such as store=true where applicable.

source_context.title: Flask testing documentation
source_context.summary: Flask supports lightweight app testing through pytest and the Flask test client; tests can call application endpoints without running a live server.

source_context.title: Privacy proof invariants
source_context.summary: Unknown scope is not completion; authorization is explicit and least-privileged; effects are idempotent; raw personal data does not enter ordinary logs; policy and legal requirements are versioned inputs; the actor performing an action cannot solely certify success; unsupported formats and failed connectors remain visible; human review handles ambiguity; audit evidence is minimized but sufficient.

source_context.title: Agent-use boundary
source_context.summary: Use one primary coding agent and at most one focused adversarial review pass. Keep rehearsed implementations outside the clean interview repo. In formal assessment, use permitted coding assistance openly and do not use hidden live transcription or covert answer generation.

source_context.title: Thirty-minute system design rhythm
source_context.summary: 0-5 clarify scope and success criteria; 5-8 state invariants and domain objects; 8-16 primary data flow; 16-21 formats, scale, throughput, backpressure; 21-26 safety, validity, reliability, observability, human review; 26-30 tradeoffs, rollout, risks, metrics.

source_context.title: Graham privacy-system bridges
source_context.summary: Use ordinary distributed-systems and privacy language first, then bridge carefully: Tau receipt-gated DAGs for independent completion proof; SPARTA/Graph Memory for source-bound governance graphs, provenance, and bounded answerability; Live Evidence for rehearsal and retrieval proof only; evidence-case receipts for chain of custody; fail-closed evals for unsupported inputs and negative tests.

source_context.title: Scenario 1: Distributed data deletion and retention orchestration
source_context.summary: Find and delete, export, restrict, or change retention for one user across a large organization; handle legal holds, partial failures, derived data, backups, and prove what happened. Probability/rank: highest probability. Domain model: PrivacyRequest, SubjectIdentity, DataAsset, DataLocation, Policy, LegalHold, ConnectorAction, Exception, CompletionEvidence. Architecture posture: clarify action, subject, actors, data universe, proof standard, SLA, then design durable state, explicit policy gates, idempotent workers, minimized audit evidence, and independent verification. Failure cases: duplicate requests, late-arriving data, unsupported formats, stale policy, partial failure, overbroad access, personal data in logs, worker self-certification, human-review gaps. Graham bridge: Tau receipt-gated DAGs and independent readback evidence.

source_context.title: Scenario 2: Personal-data inventory, classification, and lineage
source_context.summary: Continuously discover where personal or sensitive data exists, classify it, map movement, and tell product teams which policies apply. Probability/rank: very high probability. Domain model: DataAsset, DataLocation, ClassifierResult, LineageEdge, Owner, PolicyApplicability, ReviewState, UnsupportedSection. Architecture posture: clarify action, subject, actors, data universe, proof standard, SLA, then design durable state, explicit policy gates, idempotent workers, minimized audit evidence, and independent verification. Failure cases: duplicate requests, late-arriving data, unsupported formats, stale policy, partial failure, overbroad access, personal data in logs, worker self-certification, human-review gaps. Graham bridge: SPARTA and Graph Memory as governance graph and bounded answerability analogies.

source_context.title: Scenario 3: Purpose-aware access control and policy enforcement
source_context.summary: Authorize access to user data using workload identity, actor role, classification, purpose, consent, jurisdiction, retention state, and emergency access. Probability/rank: high probability. Domain model: Actor, WorkloadIdentity, Resource, Action, Purpose, PolicyVersion, Obligation, Approval, BreakGlassGrant, AuditDecision. Architecture posture: clarify action, subject, actors, data universe, proof standard, SLA, then design durable state, explicit policy gates, idempotent workers, minimized audit evidence, and independent verification. Failure cases: duplicate requests, late-arriving data, unsupported formats, stale policy, partial failure, overbroad access, personal data in logs, worker self-certification, human-review gaps. Graham bridge: Session-purpose capability policies and authority boundaries.

source_context.title: Scenario 4: Data-subject or lawful-access case workflow
source_context.summary: Accept authorized requests, find records across products, support human review/redaction, produce auditable export with provenance and safe failure. Probability/rank: medium-high probability. Domain model: Case, Authority, Scope, RetrievalPlan, CollectionJob, ReviewItem, Redaction, ExportManifest, Approval, AuditClosure. Architecture posture: clarify action, subject, actors, data universe, proof standard, SLA, then design durable state, explicit policy gates, idempotent workers, minimized audit evidence, and independent verification. Failure cases: duplicate requests, late-arriving data, unsupported formats, stale policy, partial failure, overbroad access, personal data in logs, worker self-certification, human-review gaps. Graham bridge: Evidence-case and receipt-envelope chain of custody.

source_context.title: Scenario 5: ZDR-compatible private safety or privacy-preserving ML
source_context.summary: Detect severe-risk patterns across related interactions without retaining readable customer content, or evaluate memorization/anonymization privacy properties. Probability/rank: strategic wildcard. Domain model: SafetySignal, CustomerKeyBoundary, DerivedFeature, TTLState, Alert, ReviewerView, Appeal, Experiment, Canary, LeakageThreshold. Architecture posture: clarify action, subject, actors, data universe, proof standard, SLA, then design durable state, explicit policy gates, idempotent workers, minimized audit evidence, and independent verification. Failure cases: duplicate requests, late-arriving data, unsupported formats, stale policy, partial failure, overbroad access, personal data in logs, worker self-certification, human-review gaps. Graham bridge: Fail-closed evaluation and minimization of live evidence.
